title: Refactor primitive sizing tokens and reset auto-layout constraints
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Reduce variance and accidental inconsistencies in primitive sizing tokens (spacing, icon/button sizes, row heights) and apply a consistent auto-layout constraint scheme across atoms and common molecules. This ticket covers the audit, token rename/mapping strategy, component updates (buttons, table rows, chart legends), and a safe publish plan that minimizes breaking changes for consumers.

Background: Multiple product teams have surfaced inconsistent spacing and multiple near-duplicate size tokens (eg. spacing/4/6/5 overlap across files), and several button/table components contain manual spacing layers or hard-coded widths that break when tokens change. Recent incidents show visual drift in release builds after a token sync. We need a small, targeted cleanup that establishes rules for primitive sizing, reduces variant bloat, and produces a migration guide.

Scope:
- Audit existing size tokens in the shared library and linked team files.
- Consolidate near-duplicate tokens into a single canonical naming scheme (size.XX and spacing.XX) and create mapping tokens for backwards compatibility.
- Update core primitives (button base, icon atom, table row molecule, chart legend item) to use token references exclusively for padding, gap, and min/max sizes.
- Reset auto-layout constraints: standardize on horizontal components using Fill/Hug combos and vertical stacks with fixed main axis and token-driven cross axis where appropriate.
- Compact component variants: identify and remove redundant visual variants, merge boolean state variants into single component with property-driven states where possible.
- Publish: staged library release with canary consumers, changelog, and migration notes.

Non-goals: full redesign of components, wide-scale migration of all downstream files in this ticket (will create follow-up migration outreach).
acceptance_criteria:
- Token audit completed and a canonical token mapping file published in Figma (size.[xs|sm|md|lg|xl] and spacing.[4|8|12|16|24] naming).
- Mapping tokens created for backwards compatibility and documented in Confluence.
- Button, table row, and chart legend components reference only canonical tokens for paddings, gaps, icon sizes, and row heights.
- Auto-layout rules applied to 95% of targeted components (no hard-coded spacer layers).
- Variant count reduced by at least 40% for targeted atoms/molecules, with clear notes on removed states.
- Publish checklist completed and design approval recorded in this ticket.
- No visual regressions in canary consumers after 48 hours of usage testing.

blockers:
- Need engineering support to ensure token sync script can write mapping tokens without clobbering downstream overrides.
- Legal/branding review may require keeping legacy token names for one more release.
rollout_plan:
1) Publish a 'canary' branch of the Figma library and assign 3 consumer teams to opt in for 48-hour QA. 2) Fix regressions from canary, merge mapping tokens into main library, and publish a minor release with a changelog. 3) Notify product/platform leads and open per-team migration tickets. 4) After 2 weeks of stable usage, promote to production library and communicate final migration steps. 5) Schedule follow-up tickets for remaining downstream cleanups.

Publishing checklist: bump library version, include mapping tokens, update token documentation page, link migration guide, annotate removed variants in component notes, run visual regression snapshots, request design approval, and publish with 'minor' tag.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: downstream files that used deprecated tokens may display spacing regressions. Mitigation: provide mapping tokens and a migration script; coordinate per-team QA.
Risk: reducing variants may remove edge-case visual states relied on by niche apps. Mitigation: keep a 'legacy' branch for 30 days and capture specific requests to reintroduce variants as props if needed.
